terms.comment: A post-classical transfer of the name. Stem quantities are not established and are left unmarked.
evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Coimbra: Conimbrica, -bra, Caetobrix

terms.comment: The Roman town on the site of Coimbra; Pliny names it, with a river of the same name, in the same sentence as Conimbriga (NH 4.113). It is as good a name as Conimbrica, which the town took later from the Roman Conimbriga nearby. Lewis & Short has no entry for it.
evidence: Plin. NH 4.113: oppidum et flūmen Aeminium

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
The Latin Library texts (thelatinlibrary.com), read in a local copy, for ancient passages not quoted in Lewis & Short; cited by book and section.
